subject: Vendor declarations & cloud assurance package for Acme Bank RFP

From: Alicia Mendez <alicia.mendez@acmebank.com>

Cc: procurements@acmebank.com
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: request for vendor declarations + cloud assurance package

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Thanks for the quick responses during yesterday's discovery call. As part of Acme Bank's RFP security annex, we need a consolidated package that includes:

- Complete list of subprocessors (vendor name, country, function, data access scope)
- Cloud provider assurance matrix (regions used, certifications, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM usage)
- Recent SOC 2 report or SOC attestation reference and location
- Subprocessor change-notice policy and last 6 months of changes (who, what, when)
- Sample subprocessor contract clause and proposed notice window for new subprocessors

Can you confirm you can provide the above as a single package (PDF/XLS/CSV) and an estimated delivery date? Our procurement team would like these documents to review with legal by next week.

A few helpful notes: we want to confirm whether Redwood uses any third-party telemetry/analytics providers that receive customer request payloads or traces. If so, please identify them and indicate if there is any possibility of PII exposure.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Mendez
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Bank
Alicia.Mendez@acmebank.com

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. We're assembling a consolidated package and can meet the timeline. High-level commitments below; detailed files and the change log will follow by EOD Monday 2026-03-15.

Quick answers:
- Subprocessors: we'll include our full vendor roster (infrastructure, monitoring, analytics, payments) with country and data access scope.
- Cloud assurance: we primarily run in AWS (multi-region), use Cloudflare for edge, Datadog and Sentry for telemetry, and a managed Postgres provider for backups in certain customers' Dedicated configs.
- SOC 2: we will provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report reference and an access path for redaction-friendly review.
- Change notices: Redwood issues a 30-day notice for material new subprocessors by default; we'll include our standard change-notice template and the last six-month change log.

Neha and Marissa are looped in for security and contract specifics. Laura — can you coordinate the single zip (CSV/XLS/PDF) and confirm the DocuSign/NDAs we need before sharing the SOC report?

Deliverables we will send on Monday (target):
- vendor_subprocessor_list_20260312.csv
- cloud_assurance_matrix_20260312.xlsx
- subprocessor_change_log_6mo.pdf
- sample_subprocessor_clause.docx
- SOC2_reference_and_access_instructions.txt

If Acme needs anything sooner (e.g., a phone call to walk through the matrix), I'm available tomorrow afternoon PST.

Best,
Karthik

Hi Alicia — Neha from Security here. A few clarifications and points to set expectations:

1) Telemetry & PII: our telemetry stack (Datadog, Sentry) receives anonymized operational traces by default. Customer payloads are not forwarded to telemetry unless customers opt into debug/trace exports; we'll annotate that in the vendor CSV. We'll flag any vendor that could receive customer-request level data.

2) SOC 2 access: SOC 2 Type II report is available under an NDA. If Acme can sign our external reviewer NDA (or provide an existing mutual NDA), we'll provide a redacted copy and a mechanism to request additional evidence via a secured portal.

3) KMS/HSM: we use cloud KMS (AWS KMS) for hosted offerings and integrate with customer-managed keys (Bring Your Own Key) in Dedicated/Private deployments. We'll include encryption-at-rest and in-transit details in the matrix.

4) Change-notice policy: Redwood's standard policy is to provide 30 days' notice for non-critical new subprocessors; for urgent security patches we may apply changes earlier and will notify customers within 48 hours with mitigation details. We'll attach the formal policy and a six-month change log with timestamps and rationale.

I'll prepare the security addendum text and mark any items that might require redlines from Acme legal. Expect the package Monday EOD as Karthik indicated.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.example

Thanks — that's helpful context. Couple of follow-ups before we review the package:

- Change-notice window: can Redwood commit to a 30-day minimum notice for all new subprocessors that have any potential to access customer data? If not, please state exceptions and the escalation path.
- Sample clause: we prefer an explicit prohibition on subprocessors processing customer data outside approved jurisdictions; please include your standard clause and note if you have accepted redlines on jurisdiction restrictions before.
- Telemetry: please flag if any vendor receives request payloads unredacted under normal config — that will be a blocker for our compliance team.

We can execute an NDA quickly if your DS team sends a DocuSign link. Otherwise we'll wait for the package and route through legal.

Regards,
Alicia

Alicia — thanks for the follow-ups. Quick confirmations and next steps:

- 30-day notice: yes, Redwood's default commitment is 30 days' advance notice for new subprocessors that have potential access to customer data. Exceptions: emergency security mitigations (we will notify within 48 hours) and customer-specific Dedicated/on-prem connectors where the customer explicitly manages the third party — those are governed by the customer's contractual controls. We'll include the exception language in the formal policy.

- Jurisdiction clause: our standard subprocessor clause restricts processing to authorized regions and requires subprocessors to maintain comparable protections. We'll attach sample_subprocessor_clause.docx. Historically we've accepted reasonable jurisdiction restrictions for enterprise customers during negotiation; we'll flag the sections Acme may want to redline.

- Telemetry: confirmed — no telemetry vendor receives unredacted customer request payloads under default hosted configuration. We'll highlight any opt-in debug flows and the controls available (IP-based filtering, token redaction).

Deliverables attached (zipped for convenience):
- vendor_subprocessor_list_20260312.csv (sample rows below)
  - AWS Inc., US, Infrastructure, encrypted EBS/S3 access (no request payloads)
  - Cloudflare Inc., US, Edge CDN/WAF, TLS termination only
  - Datadog, US, Telemetry/metrics (anonymized traces by default)
  - Sentry, US, Error telemetry (anonymized; opt-in request traces)
  - Segment (privacy layer), US, Event routing (only with customer opt-in)

- cloud_assurance_matrix_20260312.xlsx
- subprocessor_change_log_6mo.pdf
- sample_subprocessor_clause.docx
- SOC2_reference_and_access_instructions.txt
